questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design tenant-scoped observability without touching production logs, using a lightweight sidecar, and ConfigMap-driven routing.

## Key Concepts
- Fluent Bit routing per-namespace
- NamespaceConfigMap as policy store
- Tenant isolation and auditability
- Minimal in-cluster validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# NamespaceConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-logging-config
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  tenantID: "tenant-a"
  sinkURL: "http://log-sink-a:24224"
```

```yaml
# sidecar snippet concept (pseudo, for illustration)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnf-logging-sidecar
spec:
  containers:
  - name: sidecar
    image: cnf/sidecar:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: tenant-logging-config
```

```bash
# minimal validation
kubectl apply -f tenant-a.yaml
kubectl apply -f tenant-b.yaml
kubectl logs -l app=cnf-logging-sidecar -n tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle sink failures or backpressure?
- How would you audit cross-tenant log access?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement multi-tenant zero-trust mTLS using SPIFFE IDs, short-lived cert rotation, and KMS-backed CA in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains per tenant
- CSR-based certificate rotation with short lifetimes
- Per-tenant mesh policies (Istio/OPA) for north-south and east-west traffic
- Workload identity verification via SPIFFE IDs

## Code Example
```yaml
# CSR bootstrap (outline)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-td1-csr
spec:
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-clientSigner
  request: <base64-csr>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Per-tenant policy (outline)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-td1-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://td1/ns/default/sa/gateway"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cert revocation in case of a compromised gateway?
- How would you test cross-tenant isolation under peak load?

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```rust
// Minimal pseudo-logic for Wasm gate
fn should_allow(tenant: &str, flag: &str, rollout: u8) -> bool {
  let seed = hash(tenant + ":" + flag) % 100;
  seed < rollout as u32
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
  renewBefore: 12h

apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
```
